simple.meaning: שָׁכָה (shâkâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to roam (through lust).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Jeremiah, beginning at Jeremiah 5:8. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁכָה (H7904) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׁכָה (shâkâh) / H7904 is traced through Jeremiah 5:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7904. shakah [ שָׁכָה , so most] verb Hiph`il Participle as adjective in הָיוּ מַשְׁכִּים מוּזָנִים סוּסִים Jer 5:8 usually, horses... roaming at large they have become (compare Ethiopic ); — but meaning lustful needed; Aq Theod ἔλκοντες , Jerome trahentes (that is, genitalia ), i.e. משְׁכִים ; read with Arnheim Du Dr מַאֲשָׁכִים , i.e. fed stallions (literally growing אֲשָׁכִים , Lev 21:20 ; compare מַפְרִים מַקְרִין, ).
